required_changes.issue: The aseret-ymei-tshuva conditional is too wide. It wraps the whole Kaddish, including the canonical shared parts kaddish/yatom/yehe_shelama and kaddish/yatom/oseh_shalom. The source prints no rubric. The only Ten-Days feature in the printing is the doubled לְעֵֽלָּא וּלְעֵֽלָּא. As written, any transclusion of the canonical closing parts from this file is guarded by AYT, while the English counterparts in kaddish_yatom_closings.xml are not, so Hebrew and English go out of step whenever AYT is false or undecided.
required_changes.evidence: kaddish_yatom.xml:37-45 opens j:conditional before paragraph 1, and :51 closes it after the oseh_shalom terminating milestone. working-pages.json s355 kaddish_1…oseh_shalom shows no condition rubric. The only AYT wording is 'לְעֵֽלָּא וּלְעֵֽלָּא' in kaddish_3.
required_changes.remedy: Either limit the conditional to the Ten-Days wording only (the second וּלְעֵֽלָּא) inside the yitbarakh paragraph, or print the text unconditionally as the source does and let the place declare the season. In either case, the yehe_shelama and oseh_shalom milestone extents must not fall inside an AYT scope.

notes: Ukhetov and besefer guards are correct. In kohanim_appendix_ukhetov.xml:48-59 and kohanim_appendix_besefer.xml:48-59, a single j:conditional (holiday-aggregate high-holidays=true) holds both the instruction note and the p carrying the inline transclusion, so the rubric and the words are governed together. high-holidays matches the literal בר״ה ויו״כ / וי״כ.

Closing preface: closing_kaddish_preface.xml:47 uses only canonical inline pointers (numbers/14/17 and psalms/25/6). It adds no new Psalm 25:6 literal provider, and its declare (earlier=false, closing_appendix=true) is scoped around both pointers. The vehu_rachum mapping change keeps every Hebrew and English fragment byte-identical (s62/s63 'Remember Thy compassion, O Lord, and Thine acts of kindness…'), replacing only corresp with canonical, and both attested English wordings are kept as marmorstein_translation readings.

Kaddish Yatom paragraphs 1–3 carry only tei:seg/@source to the generic kaddish parts, with no milestone/@corresp, so no generic identity is claimed. Paragraphs 4–5 use canonical prayer-part milestones with a terminating milestone. Oseh shalom correctly inherits he rather than arc.

English closings (kaddish_yatom_closings.xml) have no publication idno and no div corresp, and carry an explicit encoding note with biblScope p.69. No new translation is invented, and Al Yisrael has no English, as intended. This file is still a literal copy that carries the canonical yehe_shelama/oseh_shalom milestones a second time in the en project, beside the p.69 file. Check that URN resolution of kaddish/yatom/yehe_shelama@…-en is unambiguous. A pointer to the p.69 provider would fit the 'callers hold pointers' rule better.

Al Yisrael: the two optional additions are encoded as separate j:conditional type="marked" spans with no substitution of adjacent words, which is correct. The printed parentheses are expected to be restored by the 'marked' rendering. Check this at export. The small unpointed (ולכון) is kept unpointed, which is correct.

Callers carry role labels in the place (הש״ץ. before Retzeh, הקהל. before Modim derabbanan), not in the transcluded texts, which follows the AGENTS.md place rule. The Kaddish role marker (חזן vs יתו, s355) and the English rubric 'The following is inserted in the קדיש דרבנן…' are absent from these modules and must be encoded in the assembling caller.
kaddish_yatom.xml replaces the printed asterisk before יְהֵא שְׁלָמָא with anchor kaddish_yatom_resume. That is acceptable as a structural encoding, but the printed mark itself is not kept.

Canonical reuse: asher_qiddeshanu_biqdushato and addir_bamarom_shokhen are used as proper identities, and the latter is attested in proper-identity-body-evidence.json. besefer points to the legacy siddur:rosh_hashanah/musaf/repetition/shalom/besefer, whose extent (no chatimah) matches the appendix. That is better than prayer:amidah/shalom/besefer_chayyim as used in shacharit_amidah_sim_shalom.xml:38, whose milestone extent includes the עוֹשֵׂה הַשָּׁלוֹם chatimah, a pre-existing extent question outside this scope. vekhol_hachayyim also uses a legacy siddur ID. Per instructions, these are not flagged for migration.
